content: 1. Gilead Sciences announced a new arm of its HIV Women’s Prevention Study to evaluate the investigational long-acting HIV-1 capsid inhibitor, lenacapavir, in combination with Descovy for PrEP. This announcement was made on their official website and accessed on October 20, 2021. 2. The Antibody Society provides a comprehensive list of antibody therapeutics that have been approved or are under regulatory review in the EU or US. This resource was accessed on April 9, 2020. 3. Laustsen AH explored the potential of monoclonal antibodies in combating neglected tropical diseases and other infectious diseases in a 2019 publication in Expert Opinion on Drug Discovery. 4. The FDA approved a new HIV treatment for patients with limited treatment options, as announced on their website and accessed on October 20, 2021. 5. Cohen YZ and Caskey M reviewed the use of broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs) for the treatment and prevention of HIV-1 infection in a 2018 article in Current Opinion in HIV and AIDS. 6. Xu L and colleagues demonstrated the efficacy of trispecific broadly neutralizing HIV antibodies in providing potent SHIV protection in macaques, as published in Science in 2017. 7. Caskey M further discussed the therapeutic and preventive potential of broadly neutralizing antibodies for HIV in a 2020 article in Current Opinion in HIV and AIDS. 8. Moldt E and colleagues showed that highly potent HIV-specific antibody neutralization in vitro translates into effective protection against mucosal SHIV challenge in vivo, as published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA in 2012. 9. Mayer KH and colleagues conducted a Phase 1 randomized trial to assess the safety, pharmacokinetics, and immunological activities of multiple doses of the anti-HIV monoclonal antibody VRC01 in HIV-uninfected adults, with results published in PLOS Medicine in 2017. 10. Ledgerwood JE and colleagues evaluated the safety, pharmacokinetics, and neutralization of the broadly neutralizing HIV-1 human monoclonal antibody VRC01 in healthy adults, as reported in Clinical and Experimental Immunology in 2015. 11. Cunningham CK and colleagues assessed the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of the broadly neutralizing HIV-1 monoclonal antibody VRC01 in HIV-exposed newborn infants, with findings published in The Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2020. 12. Corey L presented findings on the prevention of HIV using the VRC01 antibody at the HIV R4P Virtual Conference held in January and February 2021. 13. Corey L and colleagues conducted two randomized trials to evaluate the efficacy of neutralizing antibodies in preventing HIV-1 acquisition, with results published in The New England Journal of Medicine in 2021. 14. Gaudinski MR and colleagues conducted a Phase 1 open-label clinical trial to evaluate the safety and pharmacokinetics of the Fc-modified HIV-1 human monoclonal antibody VRC01LS in healthy adults, as reported in PLOS Medicine. 15. Caskey M and colleagues demonstrated that viremia in HIV-1-infected humans can be suppressed using the broadly neutralizing antibody 3BNC117, as published in Nature in 2015. 16. Chen G and colleagues presented data on the safety and virologic effects of the broadly neutralizing HIV-1 antibodies VRC01LS and VRC07-523LS in HIV-infected adults during the 10th IAS Conference on HIV Science in 2019. 17. Caskey M and colleagues showed that the antibody 10-1074 effectively suppresses viremia in HIV-1-infected individuals, as published in Nature Medicine in 2017. 18. Stephenson KE and colleagues evaluated the therapeutic activity of the PGT121 monoclonal antibody in HIV-infected adults at the 26th Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections (CROI) in 2019. 19. Zhou P and colleagues identified HIV-1 strains that are broadly resistant to CD4-binding site neutralizing antibodies, as reported in PLOS Pathogens. 20. The World Health Organization (WHO) outlined preferred product characteristics for monoclonal antibodies for HIV prevention in a detailed report. 21. Sok D and colleagues demonstrated that recombinant HIV envelope trimers can select for quaternary-dependent antibodies targeting the trimer apex, as published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA in 2014. 22. Padte N and colleagues discussed the engineering of multi-specific antibodies against HIV-1 in a 2018 article in Retrovirology. 23. Kong R and colleagues improved the neutralization potency and breadth of HIV-1 antibodies by combining broadly reactive antibodies targeting major neutralization epitopes, as reported in Journal of Virology in 2015. 24. Cohen YZ and colleagues conducted a Phase 1 study to evaluate the safety, pharmacokinetics, and immunogenicity of combining the broadly neutralizing anti-HIV-1 antibodies 3BNC117 and 10-1074 in healthy adults, as published in PLOS One in 2019. 25. Wagh K and colleagues identified optimal combinations of broadly neutralizing antibodies for the prevention and treatment of HIV-1 clade C infection, as reported in PLOS Pathogens in 2016. 26. Stephenson KE and colleagues reviewed the potential of vaccines and broadly neutralizing antibodies for HIV-1 prevention in Annual Review of Immunology in 2020. 27. Wagh K and colleagues evaluated the potential of conventional and bispecific broadly neutralizing antibodies for preventing HIV-1 subtype A, C, and D infections, as published in PLOS Pathogens in 2018. 28. Huang Y and colleagues engineered bispecific antibodies with exceptional HIV-1-neutralizing activity, as reported in Cell in 2016. 29. Cohen M and Corey L reviewed the use of broadly neutralizing antibodies to prevent HIV-1 in a 2017 article in Science. 30. UNAIDS released data in 2020 highlighting the global HIV epidemic and the need for targeted prevention strategies. 31. Brown T and Peerapatanapokin W emphasized the importance of refocusing HIV prevention efforts on high-risk populations in a 2019 article in Current Opinion in HIV and AIDS. 32. Mishra S and colleagues provided evidence to challenge assumptions about the role of sex work in generalized HIV epidemics, as published in Annals of Epidemiology in 2016. 33. UNICEF highlighted the importance of adolescent HIV prevention in a 2021 report. 34. Mittler JE and colleagues demonstrated the benefits of youth-focused HIV treatment-as-prevention efforts in generalized heterosexual populations using an agent-based simulation model, as published in PLOS Computational Biology in 2019. 35. Alsallaq RA and colleagues modeled the impact and cost of focusing HIV prevention efforts on young women and men in western Kenya, as reported in PLOS One in 2017. 36. Akullian A and colleagues examined the relationship between sexual partnership age pairings and the risk of HIV acquisition in rural South Africa, as published in AIDS in 2017. 37. 38. Cunningham CK and colleagues evaluated the safety and pharmacokinetics of the monoclonal antibody VRC01-LS in HIV-exposed newborns, as presented at the 2019 CROI conference. 39. McFarland EJ and colleagues assessed the safety and pharmacokinetics of the potent anti-HIV monoclonal antibody VRC07-523LS in HIV-exposed infants, as presented at the HIV R4P Virtual Conference in 2021. 40. Hessell JP and colleagues demonstrated that early short-term treatment with neutralizing human monoclonal antibodies can halt SHIV infection in infant macaques, as published in Nature Medicine in 2016. 41. Voronin Y and colleagues highlighted the potential of HIV monoclonal antibodies to further reduce mother-to-child HIV transmission, as reported in PLOS Medicine in 2014. 42. Sparrow E and colleagues reviewed the use of therapeutic antibodies for infectious diseases in a 2017 article in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization. 43. Brown B and Sugarman J called for updated ethical guidance for contemporary HIV prevention research in a 2020 article in the Journal of the International AIDS Society. 44. WHO provided ethical considerations for HIV prevention trials in a 2021 document. 45. Sheets R and colleagues reviewed the scientific and regulatory challenges in evaluating clinical trial protocols for HIV-1/AIDS vaccines from a regulatory perspective, as published in Biologicals in 2016. 46. Sok D and Burton D reviewed recent progress in broadly neutralizing antibodies to HIV in a 2018 article in Nature Immunology. 47. Morris L and Mkhize NN discussed the prospects for passive immunity to prevent HIV infection in PLOS Medicine. 48. Jain T and colleagues analyzed the biophysical properties of clinical-stage antibodies in a 2017 article in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA. 49. Yang Y and colleagues developed multi-criteria manufacturability indices for ranking high-concentration monoclonal antibody formulations, as published in Biotechnology and Bioengineering in 2017. 50. Walther J and colleagues evaluated the business impact of an integrated continuous biomanufacturing platform for recombinant protein production, as reported in Journal of Biotechnology in 2015. 51. Jacquemart R and colleagues proposed a single-use strategy to enable the manufacturing of affordable biologics, as published in Computational and Structural Biotechnology Journal in 2016. 52. The International AIDS Vaccine Initiative (IAVI) issued a global call to action to expand access to antibody-based products in 2020. 53. Sahin U and colleagues reviewed the development of mRNA-based therapeutics as a new class of drugs in Nature Reviews Drug Discovery in 2014. 54. Pardi N and colleagues demonstrated that nucleoside-modified mRNA encoding broadly neutralizing antibodies protects humanized mice from HIV-1 challenge, as published in Nature Communications in 2017. 55. Kelley B reviewed the industrialization of monoclonal antibody production technology in a 2017 article in mAbs. 56. Klutz S and colleagues evaluated the cost of antibody production processes in different operation modes, as published in Chemical Engineering Science. 57. Husain B and Ellerman D discussed the expansion of biotherapeutics with bispecific antibodies in a 2018 article in BioDrugs. 58. WHO outlined best practices for injections and related procedures in a 2021 toolkit. 59. The Vaccine Presentation and Packaging Working Group developed a generic preferred product profile for vaccines, as accessed in 2022. 60. WHO implemented a collaborative procedure for accelerated registration of prequalified finished pharmaceutical products (FPPs), as accessed in 2021.
